# GitHub Actions Gotchas

> Known GitHub Actions patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [Azure Trusted Signing action: credentials go in with:, not env:](azure-trusted-signing-credentials.md): the action reads SP creds from its own inputs and clobbers step env:, so env-passed creds fail auth "not fully configured"; an empty signing secret surfaces as an opaque signtool SignerSign() failure. HIGH.
- [Adding a tag trigger changes the OIDC subject and breaks Azure signing](tag-trigger-breaks-azure-oidc.md): the OIDC subject claim follows the trigger, so adding `on: push: tags:` presents `ref:refs/tags/*` instead of `ref:refs/heads/main` and no federated credential matches (AADSTS700213); pin the job to a GitHub Environment so the subject stops tracking the ref. HIGH.
- [A release workflow independent of CI publishes signed artifacts while CI is red](release-workflow-not-gated-on-ci.md): a tag-triggered release job consults nothing, so it builds, signs and publishes on a commit whose test suite is failing, and every signal it emits is green; gating via `workflow_run` cannot work when CI has no tag trigger (it never fires, and the job loses the tag to default-branch context) and querying CI's conclusion for the tagged SHA races the push and has no safe answer when no run exists, so inline fmt/lint/test into the release job ahead of the build and signing steps. HIGH.
- [Transferring a repo to another org breaks OIDC even after you update the org name](org-transfer-breaks-oidc-immutable-subject.md): a transferred (or renamed) repo switches to immutable subject claims with numeric org/repo IDs — `repo:NewOrg@259954353/my-repo@1038750424:environment:release` — so a credential rewritten to the new plain org name still never matches, and Entra answers AADSTS700213 whether the credential is absent, misspelled, or correct-but-plain-named; the obvious fix therefore appears already applied and attention moves elsewhere. Copy the presented subject verbatim from the error, add both `release` and `Release` casings, allow ~15 min propagation, and re-run the failed job rather than re-tagging. Same error as the tag-trigger entry with an unrelated cause — the `@`-IDs tell them apart. HIGH.
